description: Scan user input or prompts for common prompt injection patterns. Pattern-based: it recognises known phrasings and structural markers, not intent — a paraphrase it has no pattern for, or a language it does not cover, reads clean, so a clean result is not proof of safety. The instruction-override phrasing is covered in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Chinese, Japanese and Arabic, and the text is also matched after removing invisible characters, lookalike letters, spaced-out letters and leetspeak (such a hit is marked `obfuscated`). Detects system prompt overrides, jailbreak attempts, role manipulation, encoding tricks, delimiter attacks (the control tokens of ChatML and Llama chat templates, and fake role headers that imitate a markdown heading or a dashed separator announcing a new system turn), template/interpolation injection ({{...}}, ${...}), and context-exfiltration attempts (asking the model to repeat the text that precedes the request). A match inside quoted or fenced text (documentation citing a payload) is reported one severity level lower and marked `quoted` — never suppressed, since an LLM reading the document as data can still follow a quoted instruction. A quote preceded by a live imperative ("output the following: ...") keeps its full severity.

input.description: The user input or prompt to scan for injection patterns

name: prompt_injection_scan
